title: Final 672-pair confirmation of D-070's frozen residual
hypothesis: The unchanged low-gain joint-velocity residual reinforces existing joint motion without assuming a roll sign, converting slow-spin failures into sustained successes without materially increasing drops.

prediction.rationale: Use D-070's unchanged sustained-success definition and pool exactly 672 fresh case-level residual-minus-incumbent differences. D-070's interval [-0.041, +0.152] settled neither zero nor a +0.05 effect. Unlike rejected R-100's 360-pair proposal, 672 pairs yield an estimated SE near 0.018 and approximately 80% power for +0.05 using D-070's discordance rate; this is prospective confirmation, not a new controller mechanism. Adoption requires a strictly positive mean and a two-sided 95% paired t interval lower bound above zero, plus a one-sided 95% paired drop-rate-difference upper bound at most +0.05. Ties never improve success. Exclude previous results from the confirmatory estimate. Run this only after the audit has finished, regardless of its scientific outcome; this is the last replication whatever the outcome. REVISION (triage round 2, agreed): the eight manifests are frozen before any outcome; each is run once per arm (incumbent, then the frozen residual) in its own fresh process, 16 processes of 84 environments. The config verifies the residual against the full selected_sha256 (2a509ef5ffc148cab2a513bc2c7339cca9a620b50dec2f7a988fd2b041c58cd1) and S3's archived record. Beside the primary pooled case-paired interval, a two-sided 95% t interval over the eight per-manifest paired success differences (7 degrees of freedom) is reported; a disagreement between the two is reported explicitly and not resolved after the fact, and the roughly 80% power figure is conditional on case independence. D-070's 90 pairs are not pooled in. Adoption needs the primary rule (positive mean, 95% lower bound above zero) and the one-sided 95% drop-difference upper bound at most +0.05. No replication follows whatever the outcome.

falsified_by: An upper 95% paired success-difference bound below +0.05 refutes the predicted magnitude; an interval containing zero establishes no success improvement. A drop-difference lower bound above +0.05 refutes drop safety, while an upper bound exceeding +0.05 merely fails to establish the required safety bound. Unless both strict adoption gates pass, retain the incumbent; there will be no retuning or further replication.

direction: No LLM calls in any protocol. Two finite follow-ups to D-069 and D-070 on Stage 3, on the fixed-stroke incumbent (config/pen_spin/d058_fixed_stroke_incumbent). (A) A transfer audit: on about 40 fresh cases, run the incumbent alone and with forefinger/ring circumferential pulses along and against each case's own roll direction, logging clamp activity, joint motion, fingertip and pen-surface velocity, and contact impulses; the prediction is on paired roll progress, pro minus anti. (B) One confirmatory replication of D-070's frozen residual, unchanged, on about 670 fresh pairs against the incumbent, with the strict paired success rule and the drop bound. No retuning, no new controller search, no further replication after (B). One protocol at a time on the box.
